item.text: I’m using an explicit symbolic floating-point state: blocks record exactly which input indices occupy each live node, while a coefficient function records the accumulated factors. Each round splits at `⌈m/2⌉`, pairs by the paper’s offset, multiplies paired blocks by their node error, and assigns zero error to the unchanged carry. This separates the combinatorics from the real-error inequality and avoids assuming input values are distinct.
